input.question: why people think that being in cold weather or swimming in cold water can make you sick
input.ground_truth: Because it can. Moving from extreme temperatures one to another can weaken your immune system and that makes it easier for you to get sick. So while it won't directly make you sick to be out in the cold, going between temps is what will do it. Unless it's something like hypothermia. That can make you sick just from being out in the cold.

Question: why people think that being in cold weather or swimming in cold water can make you sick

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a little army inside your body that fights germs and keeps you healthy. This army is called your immune system.

When it’s very cold outside, or when you swim in cold water, your body has to work hard to stay warm. Sometimes, this makes it a little harder for your army to fight off germs as well as before.

Also, when it’s cold, people often stay inside more and touch doorknobs, hands, and other things that lots of people have touched. Germs like to hide on these things, and if you touch them and then your nose or mouth, the germs can get inside and make you sick.

So, being cold doesn’t directly make you sick, but it can help germs find a way into your body more easily, or make it a bit harder for your body’s army to fight them off. That’s why some people think being cold can make you sick!
